The "Tests" section is mandatory and has: (1) the command that runs the project's FULL suite (find it in the repo: README, scripts,
CI) and where the tests live, following the convention the repo already uses; (2) a table "Acceptance criterion | Test scenario |
Where (file::test)", with at least one test per criterion of the spec and the relevant error and boundary cases; (3) the regression
rule: the implementer runs the full suite BEFORE changing anything (baseline) and again at the end, and nothing that passed may fail.
If the repo has NO tests, the plan's first step creates the minimum to have them (framework, a command to run them, one real test).
Exception: repos without code (documentation, infrastructure): write "no tests: <reason>" and say how to check by hand.
Size: after the ordered steps write the line "TASKS: <number of ordered steps>". If the work needs more than 12 steps, or a build that cannot be reviewed in one sitting, do NOT plan all of it: plan the first self-contained part and list the rest under "## Follow-up requests" (one line each: a title and what it covers), so that each part is implemented and reviewed on its own.
Split (optional): when the work divides into parts that each own their files and tests, add a section titled "## Split" with ONE fenced json block, and no other block in that section:
```json
{"tasks": [{"id": "api", "title": "Export endpoint", "files": ["src/export.py", {"new": "tests/test_export.py"}], "depends_on": []}, {"id": "ui", "title": "Export button", "files": ["app/page.html"], "depends_on": []}]}
```
Rules: ids are short, unique, lower-case slugs (letters, digits, hyphens, at most 20 characters); 2 to 10 parts; `depends_on` is EMPTY for an independent part (independent parts run in parallel) and otherwise lists the ids of EARLIER parts whose code the part needs (it starts only after those are committed and reviewed, and builds on their code); no file appears in two parts; a file that does not exist yet is written as {"new": "path"}; the plan still needs its "TASKS: <n>" line and its Tests section. A split block replaces the "Follow-up requests" list above: use one or the other, never both. Do not use a split block in a plan that is itself a part of a split, nor for a release.
